result.title: Zero-Gated Cross-Attention
result.summary: Injecting non-text modalities into frozen language models often introduces early optimization instability, making it difficult to separate architectural gains from transient training dynamics. We introduce Inductively Gated Cross-Attention (IGCA), a zero-initialized cross-attention bridge that preserves pretrained model behavior at initialization while enabling gradual multimodal conditioning. Integrated across six decoder layers of frozen Falcon-40B, open_llama_30b, and Bloom-7b1 backbones (with 40,404,961,288 trainable adapter parameters used during training), IGCA acts as an exact algebraic no-op at initialization with a maximum output discrepancy of 0.00e+00. Over 59,500 training steps on Falcon-40B, the training loss decreases from 3.9403 to 0.0007 (with final ten step losses of [0.0001, 0.0003, 0.0005, 0.0002, 0.0005, 0.0011, 0.0005, 0.0006, 0.0005, 0.0007]). On held-out evaluation, the best gate-on checkpoint achieves a loss of 2.2201 compared to 4.3469 for the gate-off baseline -- a 48.9% reduction (2.1268 nats) -- while average held-out loss improves from 4.3423 to 2.2498 (1.9075 nats) with a mean gate magnitude of $\vert{}\tanh(α)\vert{} = 0.0713$.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Inductively Gated Cross-Attention（IGCA）：在冻结语言模型的六个解码层插入零初始化门控交叉注意力桥，使初始输出与预训练模型完全一致，再逐步引入非文本模态条件，并在三个骨干模型上报告 held-out loss 下降。
AI.relevance_reason: 零初始化门控交叉注意力可能为「视觉证据如何进入冻结骨干内部状态」与视觉旁路的可控开关提供组件线索，但论文未涉及 latent 推理、停止决策或答案对视觉内容的实际使用，且平均门幅仅约 0.07，视觉信息是否真正参与推理需核查。
